body.x: Airthings, a leading global technology company headquartered in Oslo, Norway, has launched Corentium Home 2, its latest innovation in radon detection. Announced at CES 2025 in Las Vegas, the Corentium Home 2 builds on the success of its predecessor and features enhanced technology to provide more accurate and actionable insights for homeowners. The device is designed to meet the growing demand for smarter indoor air quality monitoring.

Airthings specializes in award-winning radon detectors and indoor air quality monitors for homes, workplaces, and schools. With over one million devices sold globally, the company has received accolades like the TIME Best Inventions Award and the CES Innovation Award Honor. Airthings is committed to empowering people to improve their air quality and health through innovative, user-friendly solutions.

Radon, an invisible and odorless gas, is the second leading cause of lung cancer in the United States, claiming over 21,000 lives annually. Despite increasing awareness, surveys indicate that 75% of Americans have never tested their homes for radon.
“You can’t see or smell radon. Everyone should test their home to know if radon threatens you or your family. We believe that radon detection can save lives,” said Emma Tryti, CEO of Airthings.

The Corentium Home 2 utilizes redesigned sensor technology developed by Airthings engineers to deliver even more reliable data. The device connects to the Airthings app, which offers users real-time radon level updates and additional insights, such as neighborhood comparisons and personalized advice on mitigating risks.

As global awareness of indoor air quality grows, Airthings continues to lead with innovation. Over 500,000 homeowners worldwide have purchased the original Corentium Home, receiving high praise for its reliability and ease of use.
“With new studies around radon and growing competition, Corentium Home 2 exemplifies our commitment to innovation and maintaining our global market leadership,” added Tryti.

Airthings plans to make Corentium Home 2 available by Q2 2025. Additional radon insights and app features will roll out throughout the year. These updates aim to help people better understand and mitigate their indoor air quality risks at home, school, and work.

AVING News, which has covered CES for 19 consecutive years, continues to bridge the gap for Korean SMEs and startups looking to expand globally. To promote Korean startups worldwide, AVING will host its Broadcasting Zone at the Venetian Expo, featuring the CES Media Day Startup Conference and global media interviews. AVING’s international media partners will cover these programs.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host review conferences with participating companies in Korea, offering a platform for increased visibility and improved corporate image.
